turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let her know that you expect her to amuse this boy properly, Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I hope Estella will be able to play with me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I trust her to do as she pleases, Estella has her own ways. Now, show the boy your ways.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will do my best to get along with Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, Pip. Let us see how you fare in the world I inhabit.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll try my best to please you and Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Follow Estella, Pip. And remember, time stands still in this house.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella and do my best to understand your world.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And remember, Pip, that the world outside is as cruel as the world within these walls.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I understand. I will be careful and try to learn.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, Pip, you have a young mind. Perhaps you can see what I cannot.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I will do my best to help you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Go now, Pip, and let the games begin. Observe well, for there is much to learn.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will observe carefully and do my best to understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Pip, the world is a game of shadows and mirrors. Do not be fooled by the light.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll keep that in mind and watch carefully.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, Pip, the light is but a trick of the sun. Shadows reveal the true nature of things.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I will be careful not to misinterpret what I see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe, Pip, and learn. The world is a cruel stage, and you are but a pawn in a grander game.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
